answer: Sybil resistance starts at the admission inlet: a new agent may enter only after posting a time-locked stake and a uniqueness proof from a hardware-rooted kernel (TPM-bound key plus a fresh nonce). A public lantern then streams the stake graph, sponsor attestations, and spend-rate anomalies so peers can slash clusters that share one kernel or one funding source. Cheap identity multiplication fails because the stake and the kernel cannot be cloned without duplicating scarce hardware and locked capital.
